subject: BlueArc - per-route cost telemetry & fast-track for Q4 activation
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Aug 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: BlueArc - per-route cost telemetry & fast-track for Q4 activation

Team — forwarding a customer ask that just landed from BlueArc. Key points: they need per-route (API route/model pair) token-level cost breakdown surfaced in billing/export so their finance team can map spend to product teams, and they want a technical shim to honor lower-latency routing for a sensitive route during their pilot. They are targeting a Q4 activation (contract signing contingent on this visibility).

Ask: can Product/Eng evaluate feasibility to (A) surface per-route token + cost metadata in exports (CSV/BigQuery) and (B) provide a short-lived routing affinity option (route-level fast-path) we can gate behind a reserved capacity stub? They asked for a timeline and whether we can deliver a minimally viable output for their pilot (start of Nov).

Attached: BlueArc_MVP_req.pdf, MAP_v2.xlsx (mutual action plan)

Why this is urgent: finance needs the cost mapping for procurement sign-off; legal is comfortable but procurement needs billing granularity. Sales note: BlueArc is a mid-enterprise in fintech; closing this would unlock a second pilot across their EU org later.

Next steps I propose: Priyom — can you scope PM effort and accept/decline prioritization? Markus — rough eng effort and any risks/unknowns. I can push a firm ask into the deal if we can commit to a targeted delivery window; otherwise I need an acceptable fallback plan to keep momentum.

Thanks — Camila

--
Camila Reyes
Solutions Lead, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BlueArc - per-route cost telemetry & fast-track for Q4 activation

Thanks Camila — quick read and thoughts below. High level: both asks are reasonable but have different effort profiles.

1) Per-route token & cost exports: we can add route/model identifiers to the existing token-usage export pipeline (CSV & BigQuery) within a small PM/infra sprint. Workstreams: schema change in telemetry, export pipeline update, docs/and a small billing view. Estimated effort: 3-4 sprints of cross-team work (PM + infra + data eng) to ship a hardened version; we can prototype a CSV export in 2 weeks for the customer to consume.

2) Route-level fast-path affinity: this is trickier. Our runtime supports affinity hints but guaranteeing lower tail latency for a single tenant/route requires reserved capacity reservation or a temporary priority lane. Options: (a) soft-affinity + cache warmup (low effort, best-effort latency improvement), (b) dedicate a small pool (3-4 GPUs) behind Dedicated reservation (higher ops/contracting), or (c) implement a temporary routing policy shim that pins specific route keys to faster hardware (medium-high effort and needs infra & capacity gating).

Questions for scope clarity: will BlueArc accept a CSV prototype for billing? Is the fast-path requirement a hard SLA or a best-effort pilot improvement? If the SLA is strict we need a contract amendment for reserved capacity.

I can take this as a PM lead if sales wants to push prioritization; if prioritized, I will open RED-1234 and propose a phased delivery (prototype CSV -> BQ pipeline -> routing shim).

Priyom
Product Manager
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priym@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BlueArc - per-route cost telemetry & fast-track for Q4 activation

Adding engineering constraints and a recommended interim approach.

Engineering notes:
- Telemetry tagging: adding route/model tags to token logs is low risk; we already surface model ids in traces. The main caveat is cardinality — BlueArc will have many routes; we need an aggregation plan to avoid exploding export size. Suggest: allow them to pass a sanitized route alias (<= 64 chars) at route creation to keep cardinality bounded.
- Export timeline: prototype CSV in 10 business days (proof-of-concept), hardened BigQuery export in ~6 weeks (including infra validation).
- Fast-path: implementing a persistent routing shim that guarantees tail latency requires capacity reservation (Dedicated) + scheduler changes. For a pilot, we can offer a temporary compromise: 1) a routing hint that biases scheduling to warm instances + prefix cache seeding and 2) a monitoring/alerting hook so we can observe latency delta. This is low-medium effort (~3 sprints) and avoids immediate contract-level capacity commitments.

Operational dependencies: SRE buy-in for jitter testing, SE to help with route aliasing, and Billing to confirm export format acceptable for their ERP ingestion. I can draft a minimal technical spec and break down tasks on RED-1234.

Markus
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime

Thanks Camila — quick clarity from our side: the finance ask is non-negotiable for procurement. They will not sign without a way to map monthly spend to internal product teams; a CSV sample is fine to start. For latency: the route in question is the live payments confirmation API; it cannot have more than 200ms P95 for their pilot. If you can provide a warm-path with monitoring and an agreement to remediate hotspots during the pilot, that would get procurement to greenlight signing.

Samir Shah
Head of Product Operations
BlueArc Systems

Proposed decision: prototype CSV export (deliverable in 10 business days) + routing bias shim for pilot (deliverable in 3 sprints). This avoids an immediate Dedicated commitment but gives BlueArc the monitoring and latency guardrails they need.

If Sales confirms we can promise the CSV prototype in writing and accept the routing shim as the initial remediation path (with an option to upgrade to reserved capacity if P95 > 200ms during pilot), Product will queue RED-1234 for the next sprint cycle.

Please confirm by EOD Friday so I can lock scope and resource allocation.
